title: The Devil's Wandering and Job's Faith
english: Why be agitated? God commanded the worm in the morning. If the discourse is shaped in this way, such that God spoke to    the devil, do not bring forth this worthless one from a position of equality, as if he had a purpose before the Lord. The appointed order; yet the devil came and stood in the midst    of the angels, so that you might learn that while he took an angelic nature, he demonstrated a treacherous purpose.

For devil, brothers, is not a name of nature, but of choice. Why devil? For he did not become a devil from the beginning, but an angel was created; but he was named devil as one who slanders God toward men and man toward God, and as one who sets up the Lord against the servant and the servant against the Lord. For when the devil brings accusations against us, saying, 'How many evils are in the world? Where is God? Why does he not protect?' he slanders the Creator toward us; for this has been the work of the devil from the beginning.

He slanders God toward Adam, saying, 'God said that on whatever day you eat from the tree, you will be like gods.' He says that God hindered you from eating. There he slanders God toward Adam; here he slanders Job toward God: 'Does Job serve God for nothing?' That is, he is a hireling, not virtuous; he performs a wage for his prosperity; take away the money, and his purpose is stripped bare. Since God saw the righteous being insulted by that suspicion, he removes the possessions so that he might remove the suspicion and show piety naked.

And see the purpose of the evil demon. The Lord said to the devil, 'Whence have you come?' Then the proud and arrogant one, knowing neither his own rank nor the value of the one asking, says, 'Having gone around the earth and walked under the heaven, I am here.' He cries out once, desiring to show that he holds what is under heaven, that all the earth has been handed to him, and that he has all men under his feet. 'Having gone around the earth and walked under the heaven, I am here,' he said. The arrogance of the devil is cut away. For since he thought he held the image of God, he is cast out from the earth so as to no longer walk, and the Lord of all banishes him. For he is the one who promised, 'I will dwell in them, and walk...'

I will be their God. The devil wandered about. When idolatry was poured out, when impiety prevailed, and when all the things of evil reached their peak, the devil wandered about; but when holiness, righteousness, and truth are among those guarding the truth, God dwells and wanders about.

Pay attention, therefore, to your mind, he says, concerning my servant Job, whether there is no one on the earth, like him, who is blameless, righteous, true, and holding himself back from every evil? Since he said that they have gone all around under heaven, and he was boasting as if ruling all things, the word of truth parries his arrogance by saying to him: 'Did you see the man under you who has not wandered, since you rule all things, as you said? Did you see the one who has overcome all your evil? Did you see the one who struck you, the one who strikes all? Did you see the one who released your tyranny, and released injustice by righteousness, and impiety by piety?'

But he resists God and says: 'He serves you not for nothing.' Possessions were added so that he might insult his manner, so that he might insult his character, and so that he might show the illegitimacy of virtue through suspicions. You have given him, he says, abundance; take away the abundance, and the hypocrisy is stripped bare. God says to him: 'Touch all that he has.' For God knows that he has an insatiable intention toward greed; and he says: 'Behold, I give you authority over all things, but of him only do not touch.'

He limits the evil of the devil with boundaries. See then how he aims a bow against the righteous, and how he sends arrows. He went out, and first the worker of evils himself is shaped, presenting himself as an angel of evils; he himself struck the livestock, and he himself announces the plague. For the devil said to Job, he says: 'The pairs of your oxen were stolen, and the females were eaten by donkeys, and the captors came, and they slaughtered your children, and I was left alone, and I came to announce it to you.'

This is the first trial of the devil, the first arrow against the brave combatant. But Job resisted with the door of faith, which is able to quench all the fiery arrows of the evil one. The pairs of oxen were lost, and the soul was not divided. The donkeys were lost, and the noble colt the bridle of piety did not...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Arrows of God and the Deception of the Evil One
english: He refused. He saw a bitter message of the destruction of his possessions, and he remained like a secure and unconquerable tower. The devil, being bitter in his malice and bitter in his choice, regretted thus having announced it. And pay attention, I urge you, so that the thought of the Evil One does not slip from your mindsays, having observed it closely: For we do not ignore his thoughts.

As he had announced to him, that the pairs of oxen were plowing, and the females of the donkeys were in heat, and the captors had come, he saw Job bearing the message with a brave soul; he regretted that he had announced badly, and the devil said only to himself: I have announced badly, having said to him that men had fought against him. It is possible to reason that if men had fought against him and wronged him, what [is that] against God? He says, I have shot badly, I did not aim at the mark, the aim failed, the arrows went astray. I said that men had captured; this one is able to say: Why then shall I write the injustice of men upon God? Others are the wrongdoers, and another will be the blasphemer.

In order that he might transfer his mind from men to God, and show him that it is not men who are harming, but God fighting, he says to him, 'Fire fell from heaven.'n.'n.'. You cannot say that enemies threw it from above; that would insult the wrongdoer and blaspheme the fighter. Fire fell from heaven. Why do you worship the wrongdoer, why do you prostrate yourself to the one destroying your possessions? Fire fell from heaven. Job heard, and again brought forth bravely. For his endurance was truly endurance, extended until the end, concerning which the Savior says: But the one who endures until the end, this one will be saved.

Fire fell from heaven. Day by day I labored offering sacrifices for the children; what he, laboring day by day, offered, God received into sacrifice without delay. Fire fell from heaven. If I alone was clothed, I was justly grieved; but if the poor were clothed, is the Master not able to neglect the poor? I know that what he received into sacrifice, He returns fivefold. For were the possessions gathered from injustice? For did I not acquire the sheep from greed? From the fleece of my sheep, the shoulders of the poor were warmed, and the mouth of the widow was blessed.

Let him afflict me. I know what God is doing. Now, let Him take my existence as a sacrifice, for He multiplies my essence into an abundance of virtue. The external arrows do not shake me, because I am being strengthened by the internal ones; rather, the arrows of God strengthen me more from within. For the arrows of the Mighty are being struck, concerning which David said, 'Your arrows have fallen upon me.' The arrows—what kind? The arrow of piety, the arrow of righteousness, the arrow of longing toward God, the arrow of zeal for virtue; with these divine arrows the soul is pierced.

Thus, having brought upon him every trial and having stripped him of his possessions, but not having stripped him of virtue, the devil now moves against his very nature. He violates the cultivation of nature, tearing the branches from the root and crushing the children of the good combatant; he removes the fruit in order to grieve the one who begot him. And what is he doing? Look also at the message of the Evil One, how it is full of irony and overflowing with deception, capable of shattering the soul of the brave man. He says to him, 'Regarding your sons and your daughters who were eating and drinking in the house of your elder son, a great spirit came from the wilderness, and it shook the house, and it fell upon your little ones, and they died.' This word is ironic, capable of inciting grief. He did not say, 'Upon your children,' but 'Upon the little ones,' so that, having heard of the little ones, he might enter into mourning and bend in sympathy. 'A great spirit came from the wilderness.' Again, he slanders the Judge, for a spirit does not obey men, but God. 'It fell upon your little ones, and they died.'

Then Job arose; for thus it has been written. It is a good thing that he arose; for he did not fall by the plague, but arose by the power of piety; he arose and he worshiped. Worship is a reward for afflictions. Being struck, he blesses; being cast into misfortunes, he gives thanks. And he shaved his head. Now, many among us who are mourning grow their hair, but he shaved his. Why? To turn the condition of the one who is striving into the opposite form for the sake of the one who mourns. Wherever hair is honored, the refusal to shave is a sign of mourning. For everywhere an opposite form is sought from those who mourn. And he tore his garments; being drawn toward the passion by the outward appearance, but by the reality...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Unannounced Struggle of Job
english: Stripping oneself for the sake of virtue. One strips off the garment so that, like a naked athlete, he may grapple with the opponent and, through an unutterable struggle, be awarded the prize of righteousness. He who was clothed in righteousness stripped the garment; and the great singer of piety says: 'The Lord gave, the Lord took away; as it pleased the Lord, so it happened; blessed be the name of the Lord forever.' O generous soul! This voice became an arrow against the devil; he sent this voice out as arrows against the demons, shattering the phalanx of the adversaries. 'Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked I shall depart.' This voice is apostolic, even before the apostolic ages: 'Naked I came from my mother's womb, naked I shall depart,' just as the Apostle says: 'We have brought nothing into the world'; it is clear that we are unable to bring anything out. The Lord gave, the Lord took away.

He was taken from all things, so that I may cut short [the discourse], and the woman alone remained, the ancient instrument of the devil. The woman remained, not because the devil spared her, but because he kept her as a weapon for himself. For since he knew that through a woman he had brought the first man to trial, he guards the woman so that he may use a similar weapon for the attack. But there he found Adam, whereas here he does not find Adam. There he found Adam and Eve; but here he found Eve and does not find Adam. The woman says to him: 'How long will you endure?' These are truly the words of the devil. For the phrase 'How long' was the voice of one being tortured. I am being tortured, and you say, 'How long?' I am being struck, and you are indifferent to the wounds of the one being tortured? How long will you sit waiting day after day for salvation?

The devil willfully does not praise the virtue of the righteous man, but proclaims his endurance, because he was struggling in hope. 'How long?' Then see the wisdom of the writer. And having looked at her, he says, 'Job said.' He did not say, approaching her, but, having looked at her. Having looked, why? For did he not know his own wife? Did he not converse with her? Did he not beget children from her? Why then did he look? The 'looking' shows that he does not see her, but the one in her. Job looked at the devil; he saw the one speaking in the serpent, and now speaking in the woman. And he says: 'As one of the...

You spoke as a fool. Why did He not say, 'Like one of the impious,' or 'Like one of the atheists'? Perhaps He did not consider her an atheist, but rather one seized by folly. Otherwise, brothers, the designation of a fool is given primarily to the one denying God; for he says in his heart, 'There is no God.' To speak as one of the fools is like saying, 'As Eve spoke: If we received good things from the hand of the Lord, shall we not also receive evils?' O generous soul! Test his soul right there.

Job did not know that he was struggling for virtue; he did not know that he is crowned for endurance; but he simply thought the calamity was a divine act. He thought evils were coming, and thinking they were evils, he did not blaspheme as one would against evils. If, thinking they were evils, he struggled thus, would he not have struggled much more if he had known the crown? But why did God not say to him beforehand, 'See what you are doing; the devil is about to array himself against you, he is about to arm himself against you; struggle, be strong, so that he may not turn away your mind, so that he may not seize your thoughts, so that he may not besiege your soul; be strong, and do not think it easy for God to command the athlete to the wrestling match.'

For the Lord says to Peter, 'Peter, behold, Satan has demanded you, to sift you like wheat.' To the apostles, He announces the trials; but to Job, He does not announce the trials, nor the contest. Is this not injustice on the part of God? May it never be. He encourages some and abandons others. Why does He not say to him as He does to the apostles? Perhaps God knew the devil's malice, knew the envy, and knew the suspicion capable of blunting virtue.

If God had said to him, 'Watch yourself and struggle; if you endure to the end, I will give you twice what you have, you will inherit the kingdom of heaven, you will receive crowns of immortality, and the whole world will be full of praises of your body and your commendations'; if He had said these things, the righteous man would indeed have struggled, but the devil would have again found an opportunity; and if, having struggled, he had conquered thus, he would say to God, 'Did I not struggle for nothing? Promise me immortality, promise me a kingdom, promise me crowns.' Therefore, if having received the enjoyment of the temporal things, he was thought not to be righteous but merely a hireling; if he received the promise of the eternal things...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
